  required masking for those in attendance. To

  La Verne Holiday Car Show; with exception to the payment of the La Verne
  Police Department Reserves. Approved as recommended.

9.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment.

  Several public comments were received at the meeting and via the webinar.
  To hear what was said during public comment, please visit the City's website
  to view the archived Council meeting.)

  One ( 1)  public comment received by email is attached.

  City Attorney Kress replied to a question that was asked during public
  comment.  He stated that the City's Insurance carrier would not cover a lawsuit
  filed against the City on districting.

  City Manager Russi reported on the districting data on the City's website and
  that the City is waiting for State to provide needed data.

10.  Council Comments  Council Member Crosby reported on the recent passing of a very good friend
  of his,Barbara Weitkamp who was 97 years old. In addition, he reported that
  he attended the JPIA Conference and learned a lot about cyber security.
    City Council Minutes, Monday, October 18, 2021, Page 8,

  Council Member Lau reported on the Cultural Awareness and Social Inclusion
  Committee ( CASI) meeting. She reported that the Proclamation declaring
  Hispanic month was shared. She commended and thanked the Community
  Services Staff, Police and Fire for the amazing Trunk or Treat event and it was
  nice to see families there enjoying the event.  She announced that October is
  also Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis also reported on the Cultural Awareness and Social
  Inclusion Committee ( CASI) meeting.  He also agreed that the City' s Trunk or
  Treat event was amazing. In addition, he reported that he attended the
  La Verne Historical Society' s trailer of showing of their new video on " The
  Story of La Verne". The video will be replacing the Hands on History Program
  third graders Field Trips. He stated that the districting matter is important and
  that the data on the City's website is useful.

  Mayor Hepburn stated that obtaining the districting data is frustrating, but the
  City is working on it. He announced that on Wednesday, October 20, 2021, is
  the Taste of La Verne event. He urged residents to support La Verne local
  restaurants.  He stated that the restaurants were still struggling to hire
  individuals to run their businesses. In addition, he announced that the
  La Verne Heritage Foundation is holding its annual Pumpkin Patch Event. He
  commended the La Verne Historical Society for their video on " The Story of
  La Verne" and that Bonita High School Auto Shop students are working on
  restoring a 1938 International Pickup Truck owned and driven by former
  La Verne Historical President Inman Conety.

11.  Adjournment to Monday, November 1, 2021, at 6:00 p. m. for Eagle Scouts Recognition.

Mayor and councilmembers,

Here we are again discussing the traffic impacts on Amherst St.

Please find attached the comment letter I provided concerning Brandywine.

I have referred the fact that two projects were merged into one EIR document to friends and other city
planners. I have multiple AICP planners tell me that doing this diluted the facts and data for the 3717 Fruit
project.  This project should have had its own document or at a minimum its own section for analysis and
discussion in the EIR document.

There are significant concerns for the neighborhood again.

The analysis for the traffic is not complete.  There are key elements for Amherst which are never discussed or
addressed!

There is an Amherst driveway at LHS was not discussed.  Considering that is the ONLY ingress/ egress point for
busses and it is less than 50 feet from the Fruit intersection, it is staggering that this driveway was not
discussed. The parking on Amherst is not discussed and how this affects traffic flow.

Also, as the traffic study for this project again uses the data from the Amherst Project analysis, please note
that the " plant nursery" traffic count number, was actually for a commercial
  business.
The reduction taken should never have been used for a wholesale business. This is a flaw in the
document. Again, this has been pointed out in the past, but continues to be ignored.

Also,  we were able to point out, and the planning commission agreed, that the traffic study does NOT provide
realistic data.
It states that only 1 vehicle would turn right onto Amherst St.  As the ONLY way to Foothill, it is VERY
UNREALISTIC that this analysis is correct.

Analysis like this would never be accepted in other cities. It is just stunning to me what is being pushed here in
La Verne.
The complete lack of discussion of the Amherst issues is against CEQA.  OUR NEIGHBORHOOD IS

IMPACTED. YOU ARE ALLOWING THESE IMPACTS.
YOU ARE DAMAGING OUR NEIGHBORHOOD.

We are again requesting additional analysis of Amherst St traffic AND to open Bowdoin as a mitigation for
this project.

  1
  IT IS TIME TO LISTEN TO AND RESPECT THE NEIGHBORHOOD!! !  When Bowdoin was closed, there was no

environmental document, no warrant, no noticing.
To continue to hide behind these " requirements" is hypercritical.

We have two new families at the west end of Amherst. Both have small kids.  The family at Guava and
Amherst are now VERY aware of the traffic issues at that intersection.
The number of vehicles running that stop sign is increasing.  We are noticing more and more vehicles racing
down Amherst and running that stop sign.

Also note, I have gone door to door in the neighborhood and sadly, so many tell me it doesn' t make a
difference anymore. Quote " the City Council and planning department could care less about us".
 Our neighborhood is being ruined, and they have let it happen". " What has happened to our voice"

I just wanted to make sure you see these specific comments and hear these voices.

It is also noted that the planning commission brought up the driveway issue, the right turn onto Amherst as an
issue and opening Bowdoin was also brought up.

It is your turn to pause and listen to the residents.
